text.p: - About 300,000 workers staged a two-hour general strike on Thursday, protesting against planned cuts in social benefits.
- The European parliament ratified Slovenia's association agreement at Thursday's session in Brussels.
- The Slovenian governmenmt has refused to raise petrol prices, but decided to cut taxes for petrol companies.
- Slovenian Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun is due to visit his Croatian counterpart Mate Granic on Friday.
- At the end of September the number of unemployed rose to 118,083, 1.7 percent up on August, but 4.3 percent lower versus the same month in 1995, Slovenia's employment office said.
- Slovenia's only airline Adria Airways said they were considering banning smoking on all flights.
- Taxes for imported cars in Slovenia range from 47 to 59 percent and are among the highest in Europe, only Denmark and Greece have higher taxes.
- Slovenia will celebrate the fifth anniversary of the departure of the last Yugoslav soldier from Slovenia on Saturday.
- Bank Dolenjska banka increased its balance sheet assets in the first nine months by 18 percent and reached 80 percent of its planned profit for the year.
